takeaway: The portal vein forms behind the neck of the pancreas and ascends in the free edge of the lesser omentum, posterior to the bile duct and hepatic artery.

question.text: Which one of the following statements is correct concerning the portal vein?

answer.text: It lies posterior to the bile duct in the free edge of the lesser omentum.

lines.text: The portal vein is formed by the superior mesenteric and splenic veins, behind the neck of the pancreas.
It then ascends in the free edge of the lesser omentum, toward the liver.
There, it lies behind both the hepatic artery and the bile duct.
At the porta hepatis, it enters the liver as the three structures reach the gate together.
So the answer is: it lies posterior to the bile duct in the free edge of the lesser omentum.
